newsitem.title: SPAIN: Storm erupts over arrests of Basque separatists.
newsitem.headline: Storm erupts over arrests of Basque separatists.

text.p: A storm erupted on Tuesday over arrests by Spain's Supreme Court of members of the political arm of Basque separatist group ETA.

Politicians in the volatile Basque region in northern Spain criticised the arrests of Herri Batasuna (HB) leaders as serving only for free publicity for ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom), which is waging a violent campaign for Basque independence.
"They are playing HB's game," Basque nationalist leader Xabier Arzalluz told journalists. "The court appearances only serve as free propaganda for the party."

The Spanish government said the court was fully justified in arresting HB leaders Floren Aoiz and Adolfo Araiz because they had failed to make a court appearance to answer charges they distributed an ETA video during an election campaign.
Police wearing ski masks to protect their identity arrested the two men amid a flurry of media attention at HB headquarters in Pamplona on Monday afternoon.
"This is not an affair that can be judged by political merits," parliament leader for the ruling Popular Party Gabriel Cisneros told journalists.
"It's possible that HB is trying to paint itself as a victim and publically exploit the episode but the court cannot enter into these types of evaluations."
The Supreme Court has ordered all members of the HB leadership to appear and was expected to make more arrests if other members failed to show up, court officials said.

The leaders of HB, which holds two parliamentary seats but boycotts the body, do not acknowledge the authority of Spanish institutions and told a news conference after getting the court orders last month they would have to be arrested to appear.
"I'm convinced they will be released," said Begona Lasagabaster of the non-violent regional separatist party EA. "Bascially, the court is playing it just as HB wants it to."
The Supreme Court had ordered the HB leaders to answer charges they edited and distributed an ETA videotape during the campaign for a general election last March.
The video, which was played in Basque bars, clubs and schools, depicts hooded, armed rebels pleading their case. ETA has killed some 800 people since starting a drive for Basque independence in 1968.
The HB leaders will also be charged over two statements justifying the assassinations last February of a former judge and a prominent lawyer and over an internal party document.

Aoiz, the HB spokesman, told a news conference on Monday before his arrest that the court was "persecuting the freedom of expression". He said that all the party had distributed was information on the so-called "democratic alternative" to ETA.
"It's the only peace proposal that is on the table right now," he said. "We have to take steps to end the violence and for that we have to open roads that are not closed."
ETA, in a statement published last autumn in the radical Basque daily newspaper Egin, said it was willing to enter in unconditional talks with the central government.
Earlier on Tuesday, the Spanish government rejected a request by its moderate Basque allies to open a dialogue with ETA on grounds that talks would only fuel more violence.
"There are no short cuts in the war against terrorism," Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja said in a radio interview. "A hasty dialogue would only provide an oxygen balloon for the terrorists."
